title: Ten extra or ten percent extra
hook: A fixed spare count and a percentage spare count diverge as a job grows.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Distinguish a proportional allowance from a fixed spare count.

misconception: Ten percent extra always means ten extra pieces.
objective: Distinguish a proportional allowance from a fixed spare count.

claims.text: Compare an order with 10% extra, rounded up, against an order with ten extra tiles. Scaled model; quantity-only model; no installation advice.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Required=40tiles, A=44tiles and B=50tiles. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["ceil",["*","x",1.1]]; B=["+","x",10]; x denotes Required. At x=40, A=44, B=50; recall at x=55: B=65. Before ceil, resource-model.ts snaps a product within 1e-9 of an integer (snapToInteger), so x=100 gives A=ceil(110)=110, not 111 (W-357). On the slider (20 to 120, step 5) A=B at x=95 (ceil(104.5)=105) and x=100 (110); A<B below 95 and A>B from 105. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions.

claims.text: A fixed extra count stays ten. A percentage extra grows with the requirement. At forty, 10% is four; at one hundred, 10% is ten. Rounding up also ties them at 95; above 100 the percentage order is larger.

recall.question: Compare an order with 10% extra, rounded up, against an order with ten extra tiles. Change only Required to 55tiles. What is B (Ten-extra) now?
